title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood's standard processes and templates for hiring, employee onboarding, the performance & feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and new managers to ensure a consistent, legally compliant, and high-quality employee experience.

Scope
Applies to all full-time and part-time direct hires at Redwood Inference (US and EU regions). Contractors and temporary hires should follow the Contractor Onboarding addendum (link in related pages).

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
Overview: goal is to hire high-quality engineers and cross-functional teammates quickly while ensuring fairness and documentation for compliance.

Requisition & approval:
- Hiring manager opens a req in Lever with role description, compensation band, and interview panel.
- People Ops reviews role for headcount, budget, and leveling. Approval SLA: 3 business days.

Sourcing & screening:
- Talent partners own outreach; hiring manager provides 3–5 screen questions and a hiring rubric.
- Phone screen: 30-min hiring manager or recruiter screen focusing on role fit and core skills.

Interview loop (standard for engineers):
1) Take-home or live-coding (optional, role dependent)
2) Technical deep-dive (peer-level)
3) System/architecture or product design (senior roles)
4) Behavioral / leadership (manager + cross-functional partner)
5) Hiring manager final loop

Scoring & calibration:
- Use the standard hiring rubric (skills, impact, collaboration, ownership). Scores: 1–5 with guidance.
- Panel collates feedback in Lever within 48 hours. Hiring manager requests calibration meeting for candidates with split feedback.

Offers & background checks:
- People Ops prepares offer letter with compensation, equity, and start date. Offer SLA: 2 business days after approved decision.
- Contingent on background check and signed offer. Employment eligibility verification (I-9 or local equivalent) occurs before start.

Diversity & compliance:
- Interview panels should be diverse when possible. All interviewers must complete annual unconscious bias training.

2) Pre-boarding & Onboarding
Pre-boarding (between acceptance and Day 1):
- People Ops actions: send welcome email, benefits enrollment links, IT ticket for laptop + accessories, create calendar invites for Day 1.
- Manager actions: send welcome note, 30/60/90 draft, first-week schedule, and reading materials.
- Checklist: completion of KYC/background, signed offer, equipment request, and Slack invite.

Day 1 agenda (sample):
- 09:00 Welcome + HR admin (People Ops)
- 09:45 Team intro + role overview (Hiring manager)
- 11:00 Workspace / IT setup check
- 13:00 Product overview + docs walkthrough
- 15:00 1:1 with manager (expectations + 30/60/90)

Week 1–4:
- Clear onboarding goals: basic dev loop, access to services, complete required trainings (security, privacy).
- Weekly 1:1s with manager (30 min) and onboarding buddy check-ins.

30/60/90 planning template (manager):
- 30-day: learn systems, small deliverable, meet key partners.
- 60-day: contribute to team workstream, own a bug/feature.
- 90-day: lead a medium-sized project, performance checkpoint.

Onboarding deliverables & evidence:
- Completed access matrix, 30/60/90 plan in Notion, codebase PR, training completion certs.

3) Performance & feedback cycles
Cadence:
- Continuous feedback is encouraged. Formal cycles: mid-year check-in (optional for new hires), annual performance review (calendar: Nov start, ratings finalized by Dec 15). Compensation changes aligned with annual calibration.

Manager responsibilities for reviews:
- Collect upward, peer, and cross-functional feedback.
- Complete written summary and rating in the HRIS by deadlines.
- Conduct a calibration session with people-ops for teams exceeding 8 headcount.

Review workflow (high-level):
1) Self-assessment submitted 2 weeks before review window.
2) Manager assessment + narrative.
3) Calibration meeting across managers to ensure consistency.
4) Final rating & 1:1 with employee to discuss outcomes and development.

Performance ratings & consequences:
- Ratings scale: Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement.
- Needs Improvement: manager creates a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with people-ops; PIP timeline typical 60–90 days.

Career growth & promotions:
- Promotion criteria documented per level; manager prepares promotion packet (impact examples, cross-functional endorsements). People Ops schedules panel review.

4) Manager guide: hiring, feedback, and people management best practices
Hiring manager checklist:
- Complete role brief and rubric before sourcing.
- Interviewers: prepare questions tied to rubric and share pre-read.
- Decide within 48 hours and document rationale for rejected candidates.

Interviewing best practices:
- Use behavioral questions (STAR), evaluate role-specific outcomes, avoid asking banned interview questions (see policy).
- Provide fair, job-relevant assessments; do not allow culture-fit as the sole reason to reject.

Feedback & 1:1s:
- Weekly 1:1 agenda: wins, blockers, priorities, career discussion.
- Give timely feedback (within one week of observed behavior) and document in meeting notes.

Handling performance problems:
- Early coaching: set clear expectations, check for role fit. Document meetings and outcomes.
- Escalation to People Ops after 2 documented coaching cycles or severe policy violations.
- PIP process: coach, set measurable goals, weekly progress reviews, final evaluation with People Ops.

Offboarding & knowledge transfer:
- Manager initiates checklist: Revoke credentials, knowledge capture, reassign projects. People Ops runs exit interview.

5) Templates, rubrics & example artifacts
- Interview rubric (short):
  * Technical proficiency (1–5)
  * Problem solving & design (1–5)
  * Communication & collaboration (1–5)
  * Ownership & impact (1–5)
  * Cultural/values alignment (1–5)

- Sample 1-week onboarding checklist (table):
  Task | Owner | Due
  ---- | ----- | ----
  Complete IT access | IT Ops | Day 1
  Security & Privacy training | People Ops | Day 3
  Repo access + first PR | Hiring manager | Week 1

- Sample interview questions:
  * Tell me about a time you shipped a project with ambiguous requirements.
  * Walk me through a system design for a high-throughput inference service.
  * How do you prioritize technical debt vs new feature work?

6) Ownership & SLAs
- People Ops: owns requisition approval, offer letters, benefits, and compliance.
- Hiring managers: own role definition, interviewing, final hiring decision, onboarding plan, and performance management.
- IT/Infra: deliver equipment within 5 business days of start date.

7) FAQs & escalation contacts
- Who approves exceptions to compensation? People Ops lead (compensation committee).
- Who to contact for security training issues? Security & compliance team: security@redwood.example.com.

Appendix A — Legal & compliance notes
- All hires must complete region-specific employment eligibility verification. People Ops will advise for international hires and contractor conversions.

Appendix B — Revision history
- 2025-08-10: Document created (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-12-05: Added standardized 30/60/90 template (Miguel Torres).
- 2026-02-12: Clarified review cadence and PIP timeline; added sample questions (Sana Rahman).

For questions or suggested updates, please contact people-ops@redwood.example.com or the document owner.
